'''''Galium murale''''' is a species of flowering plant in the [[Rubiaceae|coffee family]] known by the common names '''small goosegrass''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> '''yellow wall bedstraw'''<ref>{{PLANTS|id=GAMU4|taxon=Galium murale|accessdate=2016-01-19}}</ref> and '''tiny bedstraw'''. It is native to the [[Mediterranean Basin]] of southern Europe and northern Africa, and the Middle East from [[Turkey]] and the [[Caucasus]] east to [[Iran]] and south to [[Saudi Arabia]] and [[Somalia]]. It is also considered native to the [[Canary Islands]], [[Madeira]] and the [[Azores]]. It is naturalised in Australia, New Zealand, Argentina, Chile and [[California]].<ref>[http://apps.kew.org/wcsp/namedetail.do?name_id=86930 Kew World Checklist of Selected Plant Families]</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Galium%20murale.png Biota of North America Program]</ref><ref>Bacigalupo, N.M., E. L. Cabral & C.M. Taylor. 2008. Rubiaceae. 107(3): 2871–2920. In F. O. Zuloaga, O. N. Morrone & M. J. Belgrano (eds.) Catálogo de las plantas vasculares del Cono Sur, Monographs in Systematic Botany from Missouri Botanical Garden</ref>

''Galium murale'' is an annual herb producing upright stems just a few centimeters long lined with [[Whorl (botany)|whorls]] of 4 to 6 oval-shaped leaves not more than about 3 millimeters long each. Flowers appear singly or in pairs in the leaf axils. Each is about a millimeter wide and greenish to greenish-yellow. The fruit is a tiny nutlet coated in hooked hairs.<ref>Allioni, Carlo. 1773. Auct. Syn. Meth. Stirp. Hort. Regii Taur.: 8</ref><ref>Allioni, Carlo. 1785.  Flora Pedemontana 1: 8.</ref><ref>[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/index1.php?scientific-name=galium+murale Altervista Flora Italiana]</ref>
